source_caption:
When the late, legendary Tim Curry originally began developing the iconic role of Dr. Frank-N-Furter for the original London stage production, he initially played the character with a thick German accent, leaning heavily into traditional “mad scientist” cinematic tropes. However, his entire approach changed after a serendipitous ride on public transit. While on a London bus, Curry overheard a woman speaking with an incredibly exaggerated, posh, upper-class British accent. He found it so wildly amusing that he immediately dropped the German accent and decided to voice Frank-N-Furter with an aristocratic, royal-sounding drawl (often describing it as a mix between the Queen of England and his own mother’s “telephone voice”), permanently establishing the character’s hilariously condescending and charismatic tone for the 1975 film.

The Rocky Horror Picture Show (1975), directed by Jim Sharman, starring Tim Curry, Susan Sarandon, Barry Bostwick, Richard O’Brien. A newly engaged, famously prudish couple find themselves stranded with a flat tire during a storm and seek shelter in a bizarre, isolated castle, where they are swept into the chaotic, highly sexualized world of a flamboyant, cross-dressing alien scientist.

source_details.title: The Rocky Horror Picture Show
source_details.synopsis: The Rocky Horror Picture Show is a 1975 musical comedy horror film produced by Lou Adler and Michael White, directed by Jim Sharman, and distributed by 20th Century Fox. The film is based on the 1973 musical stage production The Rocky Horror Show, with music, book, and lyrics by Richard O'Brien. The screenplay was written by Sharman and O'Brien, with O'Brien also playing the supporting role Riff Raff. The production is a tribute to the science fiction and horror B movies of the 1930s through to the early 1960s. The film stars Tim Curry (in his film debut), Susan Sarandon, and Barry Bostwick. It is narrated by Charles Gray, with cast members from the original Royal Court Theatre, Roxy Theatre
